definitions.explanation: One of the five digits on the hand or foot.

examples.japanese: {左|ひだり}の{手|て}の{指|ゆび}が{冷|つめ}たい。
examples.english: The fingers on my left hand are cold.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんの{指|ゆび}はとても{小|ちい}さくてかわいい。
examples.english: A baby's fingers are very small and cute.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}は{手|て}の{指|ゆび}が{小|ちい}さいから、{大|おお}きなボールを{持|も}つのが{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: Children have small fingers, so it's hard for them to hold a big ball.

examples.japanese: {指|ゆび}を{切|き}ってしまったので、{水|みず}で{洗|あら}って、{母|はは}に{見|み}せたら、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}だと{言|い}ってくれた。
examples.english: I cut my finger, so I washed it with water and showed it to my mother, and she said it was fine.

notes:
{指|ゆび} refers to both fingers and toes. For toes specifically, use {足|あし}の{指|ゆび}.

INDIVIDUAL FINGERS:
- {親指|おやゆび}: thumb
- {人差|ひとさ}し{指|ゆび}: index finger
- {中指|なかゆび}: middle finger
- {薬指|くすりゆび}: ring finger
- {小指|こゆび}: little finger, pinky

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {指|ゆび}を{切|き}る: to cut one's finger
- {指|ゆび}を{さす|さす}: to point at
- {指輪|ゆびわ}: ring (jewelry)
- {指先|ゆびさき}: fingertip

IDIOM:
- {指|ゆび}をくわえる: to look on enviously (literally: to suck one's finger)
